render.rmd <- function(file, pkg="~/github/ctsmTMB", binding = "rmd", env = .GlobalEnv) {
  if (exists(binding, envir = env, inherits = FALSE))
    rm(list = binding, envir = env)

  pkg <- normalizePath(pkg)
  html <- file.path(pkg, "docs", "articles", paste0(file, ".html"))

  makeActiveBinding(binding, function(fd) {
    pkgdown::build_article(name = file, pkg = pkg)
    browseURL(html)
  }, env)
}

render.rmd(file = "Knudsen_UKF")
rmd

\newcommand{\E}[1]{\mathbb{E}\left(#1\right)}
\newcommand{\V}[1]{\mathbb{V}\left(#1\right)}
\newcommand{\ar}[2]{\left[\begin{array}{#1}#2\end{array}\right]}

# Notation

Let the mean and covariance be denoted by

$$
\begin{align}
m_k & = \E{x_{t_k}} \\ P_k & = \V{x_{t_k}}
\end{align}
$$

# General Idea

The general idea in Knudsen and Leth's *A New Continuous Discrete Unscented Kalman Filter* is to approximate the Gaussian transition density by applying the Unscented Transform to the Euler-Maruyama discretization of the SDE. 

# Setup

Consider the Euler-Maruyama scheme approximating the path from $x_{k}$ to $x_{k+1}$ using $L$ intermediate steps i.e.

$$
x_{k}^{(i+1)} = x_{k}^{(i)} + f(x_{k}^{(i)}) \, \Delta t_{i} + g(x_{k}^{(i)}) \, \Delta B_{i} \qquad \text{for} \quad i=0,1,2,...,L-1
$$

and let the sought solution be the final iterate i.e. $x_{k+1} = x_{k}^{L}$. We can view this procedure as the mapping from the initial state value and the noise increments to the final iterate i.e.

$$
\begin{equation}
x_{k+1} = \Phi(z_k) = \Phi(x_{k}, \Delta B_{0},\Delta B_{1},...,\Delta B_{L-1})
\end{equation}
$$

We can use the Unscented Transform on this mapping to obtain an approximate Gaussian transition at $x_{k+1}$, assuming we can generate the sigma points associated with $z$. We just need the mean and covariance of $z_k$, and these are easily obtained since all variables are independent and

$$
\Delta B_{i} \sim \mathcal{N}\left( 0 \, , \, I \Delta t_{i} \right)
$$

The mean and covariance of $z$ are given by:

$$
\begin{align}
\E{z_k} = \begin{bmatrix} m_{k} \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
&& 
\V{z_k} = \begin{bmatrix}
P_{k}  & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & I\Delta t_{i} & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 
0 & 0 & I\Delta t_{i} & 0&  0 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & I\Delta t_{i} & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \ddots 
\end{bmatrix}
\end{align}
$$

The general form of the sigma-points is:

$$
\mathcal{X} =
\ar{c|c|c}{
 \E{z_k}
 & 
 \E{z_k} + c \, \Lambda_k \, \text{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_k}) 
 & 
 \E{z_k} - c \, \Lambda_k \, \text{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_k})
}
$$

where $\Lambda_k$ is a matrix of eigenvectors of $\V{z_k}$, and $\lambda_k$ is a vector of the eigenvalues, and $c$ is a constant. In this case we will therefore get the sigma-point structure

<!-- ::: {style="font-size: 90%"} -->
$$
\mathcal{X} = \left[
\begin{array}{c|cc|cc|cc|c|cc}
m_k & m_k + cQ_k & m_k - cQ_k & m_k & m_k & m_k & m_k & \cdots & m_k & m_k \\
0 & 0 & 0 & cI\sqrt{\Delta t_0} & -cI\sqrt{\Delta t_0} & 0 & 0 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & cI\sqrt{\Delta t_1} & -cI\sqrt{\Delta t_1} & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots & cI\sqrt{\Delta t_{L-1}} & -cI\sqrt{\Delta t_{L-1}}
\end{array}
\right]
$$
<!-- ::: -->
with $Q_k = \Lambda_k \, \text{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_k})$.

We form in total $N_{s} = 2N+1$ sigma points, where $N = n+mL$ is the dimension of $z$, with $n$ and $m$ being the dimensions of $x \in R^{n}$ and $dB \in R^{m}$, and where $L$ was the number of intermediate discretization steps.

We push these sigma points through $\Phi$ in order to obtain our approximate mean and covariance at the next iterate. In summary the algorithm reconstructs these as:

$$
m_{k+1 \mid k} = \sum_{i=0}^{2N} w_{i} \Phi(\mathcal{X}_{i})
$$
$$
P_{k+1 \mid k} = \sum_{i=0}^{2N} w_{i} \left( \Phi(\mathcal{X}_{i}) - m_{k+1 \mid k} \right)\left( \Phi(\mathcal{X}_{i}) - m_{k+1 \mid k} \right)^{T}
$$

## Details

Note that the first $2n+1$ sigma-points i.e. the first three columns in $\mathcal{X}$ above, all have zero diffusion i.e. $\Delta B_{i} = 0$ for all $i$. When these are mapped through $\Phi$ we therefore get just the ODE solution, and the code looks like
```{r, eval=FALSE}
f3c <- seq_len(2*n+1)
for(i in seq_len(L)){
  X[i,f3c] <- X[i,f3c] + apply(X[i,f3c],2,f) * dt
}

```



Let's pick out the first non-zero entries and define

$$
\mathcal{X}^{s} = \ar{c|c|c}{m & m + kQ & m - kQ}
$$

then the mapping is given by

$$
\mathcal{X}^{s,j}_{i} = x_{k}^{(i)} + f(x_{k}^{(i)}) \, \Delta t_{i} + g(x_{k}^{(i)}) \, \Delta B_{i} \qquad \text{for} \quad i=0,1,2,...,L-1
$$

$$
\Phi(\mathcal{X}_{i}) = \mathcal{X}^{(s)}_{i} + f(\mathcal{X}^{(s)}_{i}) \Delta t_{i}
$$
